research_question: In adults with symptomatic haemorrhoids, what is the effect of LigaSure vessel-sealing haemorrhoidectomy compared with conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy (scissors, diathermy, Milligan–Morgan, Ferguson, or another conventional excision) on haemorrhoidectomy operating time in minutes? Pool LigaSure-minus-conventional mean differences using a random-effects model.
control_label: Conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy (scissors, diathermy, Milligan–Morgan, Ferguson, or another conventional excision)
outcome_description: Operating time in minutes, defined as the duration from skin incision or start of the haemorrhoidectomy to the end of the procedure. Extract the mean, SD, and number randomised or analysed as reported for each eligible arm, assigning arms by procedure rather than column position. Exclude anaesthesia time, total theatre time, and time to haemostasis alone. Convert seconds or hours to minutes and record the original unit and conversion. Convert SE/SEM to SD using SD = SE × sqrt(n), after checking table footnotes to determine whether a reported ± value is SD or SE. When only a median and range or IQR are reported, estimate the mean and SD using an established method appropriate to the available summary data (e.g., Wan et al. or Luo et al. for mean estimation and Wan et al. for SD estimation) and document the method; when only a range is available for variability, estimate SD from the range using a standard sample-size-dependent method and document it. For multi-arm trials, retain only LigaSure and eligible conventional-excision arms; ignore stapled haemorrhoidopexy, laser, Doppler-guided, and other ineligible arms. If two eligible conventional arms exist, combine their means and SDs with standard Cochrane formulas where clinically appropriate, or select the arm best matching the review question and state the rationale. Pool mean difference calculated as LigaSure minus conventional using a random-effects model; MD < 0 indicates a shorter operation and favours LigaSure. Do not extract or pool blood loss, postoperative pain, wound healing, complications, hospital stay, recurrence, or return to work.
positive_direction: For harmonised benefit-direction coding, a positive value would represent a shorter operating time and favour LigaSure; for the explicitly requested raw mean difference calculated as LigaSure minus conventional, the numerical direction is reversed, so MD < 0 favours LigaSure and MD > 0 favours conventional haemorrhoidectomy.

vessel sealing hemorrhoidectomy conventional excision controlled operating duration
LigaSure Milligan Morgan Ferguson diathermy scissors randomized comparison
inclusion_criteria: Original randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with symptomatic haemorrhoids and comparing LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy with an eligible conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy technique.
Trials reporting haemorrhoidectomy operating time, or sufficient quantitative operating-time data obtainable from the report or authors, for both LigaSure and conventional-excision arms.

Any publication language, setting, publication status, or conventional excisional technique, provided the operating-time definition corresponds to the operation itself rather than anaesthesia or total theatre time.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.

No comparison between a LigaSure treatment arm and a conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy control arm, including studies whose only comparator is stapled haemorrhoidopexy, laser treatment, Doppler-guided treatment, or another nonconventional procedure.

No quantitative operating-time outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and SDs (including values derivable from SE/SEM, medians with ranges or IQRs, t/F statistics, or other sufficient numerical summaries); studies reporting only anaesthesia time, total theatre time, or haemostasis time are also excluded.
Completely unrelated to LigaSure versus conventional haemorrhoidectomy, or not a randomised controlled trial in adults (including non-randomised comparisons and paediatric-only studies).
moderators_to_extract: Conventional comparator technique (scissors, diathermy, Milligan–Morgan, Ferguson, or other conventional excision)
Number of haemorrhoidal columns or disease grade treated
Operating-time data handling (reported mean/SD versus converted units or estimated mean/SD)
effect_size_note: Use inverse-variance random-effects pooling of the raw mean difference in minutes, defined as mean operating time in the LigaSure arm minus that in the conventional arm. Thus MD < 0 means LigaSure is faster and favours LigaSure. Prefer a contemporary heterogeneity estimator such as REML and report tau², I², the pooled 95% CI, and ideally a 95% prediction interval when enough studies are available. Preserve the requested raw MD orientation rather than sign-flipping it. Document all unit conversions and reconstructed means/SDs and assess their influence in sensitivity analysis where feasible.
